hook: The king of the Franks who united western Europe and was crowned emperor in 800.

pages.x: Charles was the son of Pepin the Short, king of the Franks. He became king in 768 and sole ruler in 771, at 24. Tall and strong, he loved hunting and swimming, and gathered his courtiers for swims in the hot springs at Aachen.

He fought more than 50 campaigns: against the Lombards in Italy, the Saxons in Germany, whom he forced to become Christian, the Avars in Hungary and the Moors in Spain. By 800 he ruled most of western Europe.

Coming back from Spain in 778, his rearguard was ambushed by Basques in a pass in the Pyrenees, and his commander Roland was killed. Three centuries later the Song of Roland turned it into an epic, with Roland blowing his horn to call for help until his temples burst.

On Christmas Day 800, as Charles knelt in prayer in St Peter's in Rome, Pope Leo III placed a crown on his head and the crowd hailed him emperor of the Romans, the first in the West for over 300 years. Charles later said it had been a surprise.

Charles could read, but struggled to write, and kept tablets under his pillow to practise his letters. He brought scholars like Alcuin of York to court, founded schools and had old books copied. His scribes created a clear new handwriting, the ancestor of the small letters you are reading now.

The caliph Harun al-Rashid sent him gifts from Baghdad, among them a white elephant called Abul-Abbas. It walked across the Alps and lived at Aachen for years, and went along on at least one campaign against the Danes.

Charlemagne united most of western Europe for the first time since Rome and is called the "father of Europe". France and Germany both claim him, and the empire that grew from his crown lasted a thousand years.
